correctness.rationale: The line-graph identification R_{m,n}=L(K_{m,n}) turns a three-cell geodesic of length two precisely into a three-edge (not necessarily induced) P4 in the underlying bipartite edge set. A bipartite P4-free graph is a disjoint union of stars and isolates, so the selected cell family is precisely a spanning star forest. Its labeled two-sort component series is x+y+zxy+x(e^{zy}-1-zy)+y(e^{zx}-1-zx), simplifying to x e^{zy}+y e^{zx}-zxy; exponentiation yields the full EGF. Marking q column centers with >=2 selected rows, assigning disjoint neighborhoods and choosing zero/one leaf in other columns proves the finite coefficient sum without overlap. A forest with m,n>=3 must have >=2 components, equality consists of opposite-side star centers (m*n possibilities); the m=1, m=n=2, min=2 boundary multiplicities are checked separately. Independent literal geodesic enumeration gives (2,2):1+4z+6z^2; (2,3):1+6z+15z^2+8z^3; (3,3):1+9z+36z^2+48z^3+9z^4, agreeing with the package. The finite checks do not imply the general EGF.
residual_risks: Independent computations are bounded and not proofs of all-parameter conclusions.
Structural published hypotheses cited in the package remain part of the proof premises.

value.rationale: A complete two-parameter polynomial refines a previously known extremal size in a highly symmetric graph family; the natural bipartite star-forest model gives every coefficient, including maximum-set multiplicities and boundary anomalies. This exact enumeration is independently useful for metric set selection and labeled forest species.
residual_risks: Future priority discovery may revise originality; this does not make the motivated natural invariant intrinsically uninteresting.
